units.title: Bod: present
units.subtitle: Dw i, mae e, maen nhw
units.rule:
Present = bod + yn ('n) + verbnoun. Dw i'n dysgu. I learn / I'm learning.

StatementQuestion
IDw iYdw i?
youRwyt ti / Ti'nWyt ti?
he / sheMae e / Mae hiYdy e? / Ydy hi?
nounMae Siân / Mae'r plantYdy Siân? / Ydy'r plant?
weDyn niYdyn ni?
you (pl/polite)Dych chiYdych chi? / Dych chi?
theyMaen nhwYdyn nhw?

Rule: a noun subject always takes mae, even if plural. Mae'r plant yn chwarae, never maen y plant.

Yes / no: no single word. Answer with the verb, for the person answering: Wyt ti...? → Ydw / Nac ydw. Ydy e...? → Ydy / Nac ydy. Ydyn nhw...? → Ydyn / Nac ydyn.

questions.explain: First person: Dw i.
With the pronoun nhw: Maen nhw.
A noun subject always takes mae, even a plural one. Maen only goes with nhw.
Answer with the verb of the question: Ydy hi? → Ydy.
The answer is about me, so use the 'I' form: Ydw.

questions.prompt: Dych chi'n siarad Cymraeg? (No, I don't)
questions.explain: No = Nac + the verb: Nac ydw. Naddo is only for past-tense questions.
Dyn ni + 'n + verbnoun.
Question form for he: Ydy e?
Maen nhw. Also: i causes soft mutation, Caerdydd → Gaerdydd.

questions.fix: Mae y plant yn cysgu → Mae'r plant yn cysgu.
questions.explain: Noun subject takes mae, not maen. (And mae + y contracts to mae'r.)
The question form for ti is Wyt ti?
Question form for nhw: Ydyn nhw?

units.title: Negatives: present
units.subtitle: Dw i ddim, does dim
units.rule:
Negative = verb + subject + ddim + yn + verbnoun. Note: no 'n straight after the subject. Dw i ddim yn gwybod.

Negative
IDw i ddim
youDwyt ti ddim
he / sheDyw e ddim / Dyw hi ddim
(North: Dydy e ddim)
nounDyw'r bws ddim
weDyn ni ddim
you (pl)Dych chi ddim
theyDyn nhw ddim / Dydyn nhw ddim

There is / isn't: Mae llaeth (there's milk) → Does dim llaeth (there's no milk). Use does dim only with an indefinite noun. With a definite one use dyw: Dyw'r llaeth ddim yma.

options: Dw i ddim yn gweithio heddiw.
Dw i dim yn gweithio heddiw.
questions.explain: Subject + ddim + yn. Ddim (soft-mutated dim) comes after the subject.
Dyw e ddim + yn + verbnoun. (Dydy e ddim is also correct.)
Definite noun subject (y bws): dyw. Does dim is only for indefinite nouns.
Indefinite 'there isn't': Does dim + noun.

questions.sentence: Dw i dim yn hoffi te.
questions.fix: Dw i ddim yn hoffi te.
questions.explain: After the subject it is ddim (mutated), not dim.

questions.answer: Dyn ni ddim yn byw yma
questions.explain: Dyn ni ddim yn...
Negative marker after the subject: ddim.
Negative of maen nhw is dyn nhw / dydyn nhw ddim. Maen never takes ddim.
Does only goes with indefinite nouns (does dim plant = there are no children). For 'the children', use dyw.
Hi is used for weather 'it'. Oer = cold (old = hen).

questions.en: There's no bread in the house.
questions.explain: Indefinite noun (bara): Does dim.

units.title: Soft mutation
units.subtitle: i Gaerdydd, y gath, cath fawr
units.rule:
Soft mutation (treiglad meddal) changes the first letter:

p → bt → dc → g
b → fd → ddg → (drops)
m → fll → lrh → r

Main triggers

  • Prepositions: am, ar, at, dan, dros, drwy, heb, hyd, gan, wrth, i, o. i Gaerdydd, o Fangor, heb laeth
  • y / 'r + feminine singular noun: y gath (but y ci, masculine)
  • Adjective after a feminine singular noun: cath fawr (but ci mawr)
  • dau / dwy: dau gi, dwy gath
  • yn + adjective or noun (description): Mae hi'n dal. Mae e'n feddyg. (Not yn + verbnoun: yn canu.)
  • Object of an inflected verb: Prynais i gar.

Exception: ll and rh do not change after y (feminine) or yn: y llwy, yn llawn. They do change after prepositions: heb laeth.

questions.explain: i causes soft mutation: c → g.
o causes soft mutation: b → f.
y + feminine singular noun: soft mutation.
Adjective after a feminine singular noun: m → f.
Ci is masculine: no mutation of the adjective.
dau / dwy + soft mutation, and the noun stays singular.
yn + adjective: soft mutation, t → d.
yn + noun (describing): soft mutation, m → f.
Exception: ll does not mutate after yn.
Exception: ll does not mutate after y, even with a feminine noun.
After a preposition, ll does mutate: llaeth → laeth.
Object straight after an inflected verb + subject: soft mutation.
Merch is feminine (mutates after y); bachgen is masculine (does not).
i causes soft mutation.
Dyn is masculine: no mutation after y / 'r.

units.title: My, your, his, her
units.subtitle: fy nghar, ei char hi
units.rule:
Possessives go before the noun and trigger a mutation. The pronoun after is common but optional.

WordMutationcarenw
fy (my)nasalfy nghar ify enw i
dy (your)softdy gar didy enw di
ei (his)softei gar eei enw e
ei (her)aspirate + hei char hiei henw hi
ein (our)h before vowelein car niein henw ni
eich (your pl)noneeich car chieich enw chi
eu (their)h before voweleu car nhweu henw nhw

Nasal: c → ngh, p → mh, t → nh, g → ng, b → m, d → n.
Aspirate: c → ch, p → ph, t → th (others unchanged).

Ei his/her look identical; the mutation (and e / hi) tells you which.

questions.explain: fy + nasal: t → nh.
fy + nasal: b → m.
fy + nasal: g → ng.
ei (her) + aspirate: c → ch.
ei (his) + soft: c → g.
dy + soft: m → f.
ei (her) adds h before a vowel.
ein adds h before a vowel (y counts as a vowel).
eich causes no mutation.
ei (her) + aspirate: t → th.
eu only adds h before vowels; ff never mutates.
His: soft mutation, which doesn't affect vowels. Only her / our / their add h.
m is unaffected by the nasal mutation: fy mam.

questions.sentence: Mae fy car i yn y garej.
questions.fix: Mae fy nghar i yn y garej.
questions.explain: fy + nasal mutation: car → nghar.

units.title: Past tense
units.subtitle: Prynais i, es i, ces i
units.rule:
Regular: stem + ending. Stem = verbnoun minus its ending (prynu → pryn-, codi → cod-, bwyta → bwyt-, yfed → yf-). Some stems are irregular: gweld → gwel-, aros → arhos-, gadael → gadaw-, cerdded → cerdd-.

Prynais iPrynon ni
Prynaist tiPrynoch chi
Prynodd e / hiPrynon nhw

Irregular four:

mynddodcaelgwneud
Es iDes iCes iGwnes i
Est tiDest tiCest tiGwnest ti
Aeth eDaeth eCafodd eGwnaeth e
Aethon niDaethon niCawson niGwnaethon ni

Question: soft-mutate the verb. Brynaist ti? Gest ti? Answer Do / Naddo for any person.

Negative: mutate + ddim. Brynais i ddim. Formally c, p, t take the aspirate: Ches i ddim, Phrynais i ddim.

The object soft-mutates: Prynais i gar.

questions.explain: Mynd is irregular: Es i.
Every past-tense question is answered Do / Naddo.
He / she ending: -odd.
We ending: -on. Bwyta → bwyt- → bwyton ni.
Negative: mutate the verb + ddim. Formal written form: Phrynais i ddim byd.
Past-tense questions soft-mutate the verb: g drops.

questions.en: Did you have a good time?
questions.explain: Cest ti → question soft-mutates: Gest ti?
Past-tense no: Naddo.
Dod is irregular: Daethon nhw.
Gwneud: Gwnes i. Fy + nasal: gwaith → ngwaith.
I ending: -ais. -on is we / they.
Darllen → darllen- + ais.
Negative of ces i: Ches i ddim (Ges i ddim is also heard).

units.title: Cyn i, ar ôl i, rhaid i
units.subtitle: cyn i fi golli'r bws
units.rule:
Equation: cyn / ar ôl / wrth / nes / er mwyn + i + person + soft-mutated verbnoun.

cyn i fi golli'r bws = before I miss the bus.

i fii ni
i tii chi
iddo fe / iddi hiiddyn nhw
with a noun: i'r bws, i Siân

No tense of its own. The main clause sets the time: Gadawais i cyn iddo fe gyrraedd (before he arrived). Bydda i'n gadael cyn iddo fe gyrraedd (before he arrives).

cyn ibefore
ar ôl iafter
wrth ias / while
nes iuntil
er mwyn iso that

Rhaid i (must) works the same: Rhaid i fi fynd.

Shortcuts: same subject in both halves → drop i + person: Bwytais i cyn mynd. Before a plain noun → no i: cyn y cyfarfod, ar ôl cinio.

questions.en: I must go before I miss the bus.
questions.answer: Rhaid i fi fynd cyn i fi golli'r bws
questions.explain: Rhaid i fi + soft (fynd); cyn i fi + soft (golli).
i + person + soft mutation: m → f.
i inflects for he: iddo fe. Then soft mutation: cyrraedd → gyrraedd.
i + person + soft mutation: c → g.
Before a plain noun (no verb), no i: cyn y cyfarfod.

questions.answer: Gadawais i cyn iddi hi gyrraedd
questions.explain: Iddi hi + soft mutation. The past meaning comes from Gadawais.

questions.sentence: Ar ôl i ni bwyta, aethon ni allan.
questions.fix: Ar ôl i ni fwyta, aethon ni allan.
questions.explain: The verbnoun after i + person soft-mutates: bwyta → fwyta.

questions.sentence: Cyn dw i'n mynd adre, rhaid i fi siopa.
questions.fix: Cyn i fi fynd adre, rhaid i fi siopa.
questions.explain: No normal tense after cyn. Use i + person + mutated verbnoun.

questions.prompt: Wrth i fi gerdded adre, dechreuodd hi fwrw glaw.
options: As I was walking home, it started to rain.
Before I walked home, it started to rain.
After I walked home, it started to rain.
questions.explain: Wrth i = as / while.
Nes i = until. Soft mutation: d → dd.
Iddyn nhw + soft mutation: gadael → adael (g drops).
Same subject in both halves: cyn + verbnoun, no i and no mutation.
